sinusoidal alterations are a common finding in liver biopsied and are often not related to primary hepatocytic damage.

sinusoidal alterations can be the first signs of liver cell damage, can be the cause of liver cell damage or can be the result of liver cell damage.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sinusoids and the perisinusoids are important structures for liver pathologists and that they should be carefully examined in liver biopsys.
sinusoidal alterations can occur in a wide range of liver diseases, and that the knowledge of their morphologic appearance is important for the diagnosis and understanding of liver diseases.
liver biopsy can be a very helpful tool in the diagnosis of rare and uncommon diseases of the liver and the liver sinusoids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sinusoidal endothelial cells play a critical role in the regulation of hepatic microvascular perfusion and function.
the sinusoidal endothelial cells are not just a passive filter for blood flow, but they are an important component of liver function and are involved in the pathogenesis of liver disease.
the sinusoids are a highly dynamic and complex organ, with many different cell populations, including endothelial cells, Kupffer cells, stellate cells, and lymphocytes.
